blocks.text: The Narration of Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) about what he Memorised from Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Narration of Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) about the Knowledge of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)
Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) says, "I have learnt a thousand similitudes from Rasulullaah ﷺ." [^2]

In a lengthy narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Whenever they (the Sahabah (RA)) disagreed about anything, my father (Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)) would come forth with a Hadith that would satisfy them all and settle the dispute. Therefore, when it was asked where Rasulullaah ﷺ was to be buried, no one could be found who had any relevant knowledge. It was then that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, 'I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Whenever a Nabi (AS) passed away, he was buried beneath the place he lay at the time he passed away.' Similarly, when the Sahabah (RA) posed divergent opinions about the inheritance of Rasulullaah ﷺ, they could find none with relevant knowledge. Again it was Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) who said, 'I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'We the assembly of Ambiyaa do not leave behind any inheritance. Everything we leave behind is donated as Sadaqah.'" [^3]
The Statements of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) and Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) About the Knowledge of Hadhrat Umar (RA)

Hadhrat Abu Waa'il narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "If the knowledge of Umar (RA) was placed on one pan of a scale and the knowledge of all on earth was placed on the other, the knowledge of Umar (RA) would outweigh the rest." Hadhrat A'mash says, "I found it difficult to accept this, so I mentioned it to Ibraheem, who said, 'Why do you find this difficult to accept when I can swear by Allaah that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said something even more profound than this. He said, 'In my estimation, nine tenths of knowledge left the world with the demise of Umar (RA).'" [^4]
